task: Task 9 — deterministic romanization folding + aliases for retrieval ONLY

policy.retrieval_only: Applied to the BM25 index text and to queries. Never applied to corpus files; returned results always expose the original released text and full provenance.
policy.no_stemming: Stemming would merge distinct religious/philosophical terms (e.g. 'sutra'/'sutrakritanga').
policy.no_fuzzy_matching: Soundex/metaphone-style matching would merge distinct Prakrit/Sanskrit/Indic words.
policy.orthographic_only: Mapping two spellings is an ORTHOGRAPHIC equivalence for search. It never asserts religious, textual, or canonical equivalence between works, recensions, or traditions.
policy.evidence_bar: Every entry must be justified by existing corpus text, Task 8 evaluation queries, or manifest/source metadata. Variants without such evidence are listed under rejected_variants.

folding.description: Deterministic one-directional Latin diacritic folding for Latin-script tokens. Unconditional (script-verified by construction), reversible: no, idempotent: yes. Kept minimal: vowel/retroflex/nasal/honorific letters as observed in corpus titles ('Sthānakavāsī' vs 'Sthanakvasi', 'Tattvārtha' vs 'Tattvartha').
folding.applied_to: Latin-script tokens only. Indic-script (Devanagari/Gujarati) tokens are passed through untouched; no cross-script transliteration is attempted (no evidence base for it in this task).

alias_groups.reason: Gujarati 'Jain dharma'. Corpus uses the compound જૈનધર્મ (5 units) and the spaced જૈન ધર્મ (2 units) in the same sources; 'જેનધરમ' is the no-virama spelling of the compound, attested once inside the phrase 'જેનધરમનું' (SVK-2012, sect-critical sentence). Mapped in BOTH directions: a compound query reaches spaced docs and a spaced query reaches compound docs. Phrase mechanism guarantees fragments ('જૈન', 'ધર્મ' alone) never become alias keys.
alias_groups.corpus_occurrences: જૈનધર્મ 5 units; જૈન ધર્મ 2 units; જેનધરમ 1 unit (SVK-2012); જેન ધર્મ 0 — added for query-side coverage of the no-virama system

alias_groups.reason: Historical/OCR spelling WITHOUT virama: 'ધરમ' occurs 29 units, concentrated in SVK-2012 (12) and SVK-2014 (11) where contexts are unambiguous 'dharma' prose ('ધરમની વ્યાખ્યામાં', 'વીર પરમાત્માનું નામ એ ધરમ બનાવી દેશે'); the isolated ધરમ token cannot be a substring false-positive (it contains no combining signs). In OCR-heavy dictionary sources (SVK-2002/2003/2004) ધરમ appears only INSIDE garbled longer strings (ઉંધરમા, મધરમ, શકેરધરમાં) — different tokens, unaffected by an exact-token alias. Full context list preserved in task10 report.
alias_groups.corpus_occurrences: ધરમ 29 units (SVK-2012 12, SVK-2014 11, dictionaries 6) vs ધર્મ 242 units

alias_groups.reason: Standard Sanskrit transliteration 'Sūtrakṛtāṅga' → folded 'sutrakrtanga'; the older/looser romanization 'Sutrakritanga' occurs in user queries (Task 8 q3 'Sutrakritanga' failed against a corpus using 'Sutrakrtanga').
alias_groups.corpus_occurrences: Sutrakrtanga 4868 units; Sutrakritanga 1 unit (release JSONL grep, 2026-09-18)

alias_groups.reason: Historical romanization 'Utradhyayan' (colonial-era orthography, vowel deletion) vs standard 'Uttaradhyayana'. Task 8 q5 'Uttaradhyayana Sutra' under-recalled against corpus text using 'Utradhyayan'.
alias_groups.corpus_occurrences: Utradhyayan 1984 units; Uttaradhyayana 5 units (release JSONL grep, 2026-09-18)

alias_groups.reason: Prakrit title form 'Uttarajjhayana' vs Sanskritized 'Uttarādhyayana'. Both spellings occur in the corpus (Prakrit-grammar/dictionary contexts), so a query using either form should reach units using the other. Same canonical text title, different script-era romanization — orthographic mapping only.
Muni Ratnachandra (lexicographer, Task 8 q9) is named in the corpus overwhelmingly as 'Ratnachandraji' (honorific fused into one token). A query 'Ratnachandra' must reach those units.

Task 8's documented failure mode 'Ratnachandra vs Ratna Chandra Ji': the fully spaced form with honorific tokenizes as three tokens ('ratna','chandra','ji') and matches nothing, because the corpus fuses 'Ratnachandraji' into one token. Phrase rule: the contiguous sequence injects the fused term; the parts themselves never become keys or index terms.
alias_groups.corpus_occurrences: spaced 'Ratna Chandra' occurs 0 times in the release (grep, 2026-09-18) — the expansion covers the spaced+honorific query form only

rejected_variants.reason: DIFFERENT LEXEMES. All 24 corpus occurrences of 'જયન' are inside 'વિજયની' (victory; city names like Vijayapuri) or OCR numerics (SVK-2002/2003, context-inspected 2026-09-18). Merging would summon victory/city passages for 'Jain' queries.

Distinct words ('જિન' = Jina/conqueror, 'જૈન' = Jain) — never merged. The Task 10 tokenizer fix REMOVED the pre-existing accidental collision (both collapsed to identical fragments ['જ','ન'] under the old combining-mark-dropping tokenizer); they are now correctly distinct tokens.
There ધરમ appears only as a substring of OCR-garbled longer strings (ઉંધરમા, મધરમ, શકેરધરમાં) — different tokens unaffected by an exact-token alias; no standalone dharma usage found there.
0 occurrences in the corpus — no evidence; the derivational morphology of Gujarati is NOT aliased (would be unbounded stemming).

Different romanization systems (English catalog vs Gujarati transliteration) naming DIFFERENT works/editions; no corpus evidence they refer to the same text string, and merging them risks conflating distinct sources (SVK-2010 vs sect references). Not evidenced as an orthographic equivalence.
No Task 8 failure demonstrates it; would risk merging unrelated terms.
Handled only inside the evidenced ratnachandraji groups; a global rule could merge unrelated personal names.
No evidence base compiled in this task; explicitly out of scope.

apply_at.index: BM25Index builds its token map over folded tokens and adds alias expansions of every folded term in the document.
apply_at.query: BM25Index.search folds the query and expands each folded query token through the alias map before scoring.
apply_at.results: Returned documents are the ORIGINAL RetrievalDocument objects — text, locator, provenance and religious_scope are untouched.
